\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بکنگ} (buking)}{بکنگ (buking)}]{\ur{بکنگ} (buking) — a booking}

\label{lesson:UR-C391-buking}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for cancelled, then the Urdu for to take down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بکنگ}}
\textbf{\ur{بکنگ}} — \emph{buking} — \textquotedblleft{}a booking\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{کل} \ur{ٹکٹ} \ur{کی} \ur{بکنگ} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne kal ṭikaṭ kī buking kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I booked the ticket yesterday.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بکنگ}} (\emph{buking}) is borrowed from English \emph{booking}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buking}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buking}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maiṅ ne kal ṭikaṭ kī buking kī.} — I booked the ticket yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for cancelled, then the Urdu for to take down, then say \emph{buking} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قطار} (qatār)}{قطار (qatār)}]{\ur{قطار} (qatār) — a queue; a row}

\label{lesson:UR-C391-qatar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to take down, then the Urdu for a booking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قطار}}
\textbf{\ur{قطار}} — \emph{qatār} — \textquotedblleft{}a queue; a row\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ٹکٹ} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{لمبی} \ur{قطار} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭikaṭ ke liye lambī qatār thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a long queue for tickets.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qiṭār}, \textquotedblleft{}a line of camels\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu any line of people waiting is a \textbf{\ur{قطار}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to take down, then the Urdu for a booking, then say \emph{qatār} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رش} (rash)}{رش (rash)}]{\ur{رش} (rash) — a rush (of people); a crowd}

\label{lesson:UR-C391-rash}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a queue, then the Urdu for a counter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رش}}
\textbf{\ur{رش}} — \emph{rash} — \textquotedblleft{}a rush (of people); a crowd\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{صبح} \ur{کے} \ur{وقت} \ur{اسٹیشن} \ur{پر} \ur{رش} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{subah ke vaqt isṭeshan par rash hotā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The station is very crowded in the mornings.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

Everyday spoken Urdu; news reports and notices write \ur{ہجوم} (hujūm), \textquotedblleft{}a crowd\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رش}} (\emph{rash}) is borrowed from English \emph{rush}; in Urdu it names the crowd itself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rash}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{subah ke vaqt isṭeshan par rash hotā hai.} — The station is very crowded in the mornings.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a queue, then the Urdu for a counter, then say \emph{rash} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گھسنا} (ghusnā)}{گھسنا (ghusnā)}]{\ur{گھسنا} (ghusnā) — to push in; to squeeze in}

\label{lesson:UR-C391-ghusna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a counter, then the Urdu for a rush (of people).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گھسنا}}
\textbf{\ur{گھسنا}} — \emph{ghusnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to push in; to squeeze in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ایک} \ur{آدمی} \ur{قطار} \ur{میں} \ur{آگے} \ur{گھس} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ek ādmī qatār meṅ āge ghus gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A man pushed in near the front of the queue.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{ڈبے} \ur{میں} \ur{گھس} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh ḍabbe meṅ ghus gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گھسنا}} (\emph{ghusnā}) is inherited from \emph{ghuss}, \textquotedblleft{}thrust in\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 4492).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghusnā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a counter, then the Urdu for a rush (of people), then say \emph{ghusnā} again
\end{itemize}
